AK RAIL NETWORK - SIGNALLING AND TRACK MAINTENANCE STANDARD STD-217

Section 4: Curve 47
Curve 47 on the Down Main between mile markers 14 and 15 carries a permanent speed restriction. For conventional trains, the maximum permitted speed over Curve 47 is 95 km/h. Tilting trains fitted with an approved tilt system may pass over Curve 47 at a maximum permitted speed of 105 km/h. Expressed in imperial units, the conventional limit is 59 mph and the tilting-train limit is 65 mph. The applied cant through Curve 47 is 150 mm. The cant deficiency permitted through Curve 47 is 110 mm.

Section 5: Gradient Section 12
Gradient Section 12 climbs away from North Junction toward the summit. The gradient is expressed in the traditional notation as 1 in 80. In the equivalent percentage notation used on the electronic gradient profile, Gradient Section 12 is graded at 1.25%.

Section 6: North Junction
North Junction is laid to standard gauge throughout. The track gauge at North Junction is 1435 mm.

Section 7: Signal SB204
Signal SB204 protects the approach to Platform 3 Crossover. The required braking distance on the approach to Signal SB204 is 1200 m. The minimum sighting time for Signal SB204 is 12 seconds. Signal SB204 is a four-aspect colour light signal.

Section 8: Bridge 88
Bridge 88 carries the Down Main over the river on a steel through-girder structure. The maximum axle load permitted on Bridge 88 is 25 tonnes.

Section 9: Viaduct 22
Viaduct 22 is a masonry structure dating from 1932 with twelve arches. The maximum axle load permitted on Viaduct 22 is 22.5 tonnes.

Section 10: Level Crossing 9
Level Crossing 9 is an automatic half-barrier crossing on the branch line. The controlling authority for Level Crossing 9 is Network Control North.

Section 11: Tunnel Section 4
Tunnel Section 4 passes beneath the summit ridge for approximately 900 metres. The maximum permitted speed through Tunnel Section 4 is 60 km/h.

All speeds, gradients, gauges, braking distances, axle loads, sighting times and cant values in this standard are binding on maintenance and signalling staff.
